titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 39: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 39. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number ⲗⲑ (top right) is printed with a bar above and below as the frame, not as a supralinear stroke. Stroke over the first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲉϥⲣⲱⲙⲉ only (716–728); the stroke over ϩ of ⲉϥⲧⲱⲃϩ is printed obliquely (952–959).

Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲣⲱⲙⲉ (779–791), ⲛ of ϩⲛ (1035–1047) and ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (1174–1187). Four sublinear dots under ⲁⲓⲛⲉ (x 1249–1292).
Bars detected at 577–587 and 914–923 are the top of ⲃ and the hook of ϭ (6×), not strokes. Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛϩⲏⲧ[ⲟ]ⲩ (1057–1070).

The stroke over ϩ of ⲛϩ is printed obliquely (566–572). Stroke over ⲙ of ϩⲙ (869–882). The dot is under ⲕ of ⲙⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ (x 1115), not ⲉ.
Strokes over the first ⲙ of ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ (679–692), ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁⲥ (1143–1156) and the final ⲛ (1229–1242); a bar at 850–859 is the top of ⲃ (6×).
Stroke over ⲙ of ϩⲙ (1025–1039).
Stroke over the final ⲙ (1263–1276), which also carries a dot (x 1267). The bar at 690–698 is the top of ϯ.

After ⲙⲡⲓⲱⲧ and a blank of 64 px, the edition prints a free-standing cross (x 1303–1326, y 1020–1048) with equal arms and the bar at mid-height. It is 23 px wide against 17 px for ϯ on this page (l. 14) and stands apart from any word, so it is read as a printed sign, not as the letter ϯ, and encoded as a sign of type cross (ledger §7); the blank before it is encoded as an unmarked blank.
